spec_provided_observability.name: Parity bit P (bit 31 of each subframe)
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Even parity over bits 4-30; receiver may report any mismatch, providing per-subframe error detection.

spec_provided_observability.name: Validity bit V (bit 28 of each subframe)
spec_provided_observability.purpose: V = 0 → sample valid for D/A; V = 1 → sample not valid (e.g. IEC 61937 carrier or fault). Receiver can report V transitions as a coarse error indicator.

spec_provided_observability.name: X / Y / Z preamble pattern
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Loss of expected preamble periodicity signals loss of BMC lock or subframe alignment, useful for receiver lock-status reporting.

spec_provided_observability.name: Channel-status byte 0 bit 0 (Consumer / Professional)
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Receiver can verify the link is in the expected mode (Consumer = S/PDIF). Mismatch indicates either misconfigured transmitter or wrong-type cable / interface.

spec_provided_observability.name: Channel-status byte 3 sampling frequency code
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Receiver can compare declared rate (44.1 / 48 / 32 / 88.2 / 96 / 176.4 / 192 kHz) against measured BMC rate; mismatch indicates channel-status corruption or transmitter misconfiguration.

spec_provided_observability.name: Channel-status byte 4 word-length code
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Lets receiver decide how many LSBs of the 20-bit audio field carry meaningful data (and whether to use the Aux field for the 21-24 LSBs of a 24-bit sample).

spec_provided_observability.name: Receiver-measured jitter
spec_provided_observability.purpose: S/PDIF is widely known to inject jitter into recovered clocks; measuring jitter at the recovered clock or downstream DAC clock identifies link quality.

notes: IEC 60958 does not specify a formal observability architecture beyond V / P / preamble / channel-status. Concrete S/PDIF receiver IPs typically expose: lock-status, BMC bit-error counter, parity-error counter, validity-fault counter, channel-status snapshot register, IEC 61937 bitstream-type detect, sample-rate measurement, and jitter accumulator — all per-implementation and beyond the IEC 60958 normative content.
